sections.h2: Where is Champaign and why does the university matter to home sellers?
sections.html:
Champaign is a city in Champaign County in east-central Illinois, and it shares the main University of Illinois campus with its twin city, Urbana. The 2020 census counted 88,302 residents, making it the tenth most populous municipality in the state and the fourth largest outside the Chicago area.

The university is the biggest fact in the local housing market. The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign enrolls more than 50,000 students a year, and Parkland College adds about 9,000. Whether a house sits near campus, near Parkland on the northwest side or out toward the newer southwest subdivisions changes who the likely buyer or tenant is.

  • City area: 22.99 square miles of land, with Urbana on its eastern border
  • Metro: the Champaign-Urbana area had about 236,000 residents in 2020
  • Oldest surviving building: the Cattle Bank, built in 1858

The city dates to 1855, when the Illinois Central Railroad laid its track two miles west of downtown Urbana. The new town was first called West Urbana and took the name Champaign when it received a city charter in 1860. The name comes from Champaign County, Ohio, which took it from a French word for open, level country.

The flat prairie location matters for houses today. Champaign sits on relatively high ground for the region, and downtown drains toward Boneyard Creek. Ask your insurer or the city about drainage if your street is near the creek, since a buyer's inspector will notice a wet basement.

sections.html:
Public institutions and health care dominate. The Champaign County Economic Development Corporation's top ten list, as summarized by the encyclopedia entry for the city, is below.

The university's Research Park, just south of the State Farm Center, hosts technology firms, and the EnterpriseWorks incubator has launched more than 350 startups since 2014. Wolfram Research is the largest high-technology employer in town, with more than 400 local employees. A mix of university, hospital and technology jobs tends to keep demand for housing steady in good and weak years.

sections.h2: What are Campustown and downtown Champaign like for property owners?
sections.html:
Campustown, along Green Street, is the retail and entertainment district for students. Streetscape work finished around 2002 and was followed by high-rise apartment buildings, including the 18-story Burnham 310 and the 24-story 309 Green, both opened in 2008, and a 14-story complex finished in 2014 at Sixth and Green.

Downtown Champaign is a separate district around City Building and the Virginia Theatre, a restored 1,463-seat theater that opened on December 28, 1921. In the 1980s a section of Neil Street was closed to cars as a pedestrian mall, but business declined and the experiment ended. Later mixed-use buildings and a city-funded parking deck helped revive the area. A single-family seller a few blocks from either district should expect buyers to ask about parking, noise and nearby rental density.

sections.h2: How do Champaign winters and summers affect an older house?
sections.html:
Champaign has a humid continental climate with hot summers and cold winters. The city averages 40.92 inches of precipitation and 20.8 inches of snow a year. Temperatures top 90 degrees on about 24 days a year and fall below zero on about six nights.

  • Record high: 109 degrees in 1954; record low: minus 25, hit on four separate occasions
  • Wettest months: May and June, at about 4.8 and 4.6 inches of rain
  • Snowiest months: January, 6.5 inches, and February, 5.8 inches

Those swings put stress on roofs, gutters, sump pumps, furnaces and air conditioners in the same year. Buyers' inspectors in Champaign tend to look at all four, so a seller with an aging system can expect the issue to surface in negotiations. A cash buyer purchasing as-is usually prices that in directly.

sections.h2: Which schools and districts serve Champaign homes?
sections.html:
Champaign Unit 4 School District serves the city and runs Champaign Central High School and Champaign Centennial High School. Private options include St. Thomas More High School on the northwest side, Judah Christian School just south of Interstate 74 on Prospect Avenue, and Academy High in south Champaign.

Parkland College, in northwestern Champaign, is part of the Illinois Community College System. Homes near Parkland or the university draw a different group of buyers than homes inside the Unit 4 attendance areas, so check the attendance boundary before you advertise a school connection.

sections.h2: What roads, rail and airport serve Champaign?
sections.html:
Interstates 57, 72 and 74 all meet at or near Champaign. I-57 and I-72 meet in a cloverleaf, I-72 heads toward Decatur and ends at University Avenue on the southeast side, and I-74 leads to Indianapolis. U.S. 45 and U.S. 150 also serve the area.

Illinois Terminal, opened in 1999, is the intermodal hub for Amtrak, intercity buses and the local Champaign-Urbana Mass Transit District. Amtrak stops here with the City of New Orleans, the Saluki and the Illini. The university also operates Willard Airport. Houses near a bus line to campus are easy to describe to investors and to students' parents.

sections.h2: What does the City of Champaign require for building work and rentals?
sections.html:
Permits are needed to build, enlarge, alter, repair, move or demolish a building, or to install or replace electrical, gas, mechanical, plumbing, sprinkler or fire alarm systems. Sheds up to 120 square feet, fences (zoning rules still apply), playground equipment and minor repairs are exempt. Since January 1, 2025, applications go through an online portal. The city adopted the 2021 International Codes on January 9, 2024.

The Neighborhood Code Compliance Division enforces property maintenance, nuisance and blight rules, and residents can file a complaint with the city. The city's rental registration page describes a proposed registry of residential rentals and vacant commercial buildings meant to give the city current owner and agent contact information. If you own a rental, ask the Neighborhood Services department whether registration has taken effect.

Downtown property owners should know about the snow rule. When public works declares the ordinance in effect after more than two inches of snow, owners in the designated areas have 24 hours to clear sidewalks, or the city clears them and bills the owner plus an administrative fee.

sections.h2: What do the state and county require when I sell a Champaign house?
sections.html:
Illinois imposes a transfer tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated on the declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). The declaration is filed through the state's MyDec system, whose customer service line is 844-445-1114.

The deed is recorded with the Champaign County recorder. Ask the county recorder, the City of Champaign and your title company whether any local transfer or utility requirement applies to your property before the closing date is set.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell it myself or take a cash offer in Champaign?
sections.html:
A listing usually fits a well-kept house that can wait through a school-year showing schedule. A house with deferred repairs or a student-oriented rental may suit an as-is sale to a buyer who plans to fix it up. A cash offer shortens the timeline and removes repair negotiations, at the cost of a price below a fully renovated sale.

Whichever route you choose, gather the permit history, utility information and any tenant lease before you talk to buyers.

faqs.q: What is the largest employer in Champaign?
faqs.a: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, with 13,934 employees on the Champaign County Economic Development Corporation list. Carle Foundation Hospital is second with 6,921.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a shed or fence in Champaign?
faqs.a: Sheds up to 120 square feet and fences are exempt from building permits, but zoning rules still apply to fences. Ask the Building Safety Division before you build.

faqs.q: How do I report a property maintenance problem?
faqs.a: File a complaint with the Neighborhood Code Compliance Division of the City of Champaign. The division enforces property maintenance, nuisance and blight rules.

faqs.q: What is the Illinois transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The state rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the transfer declaration. The declaration is completed in the state's MyDec system.

faqs.q: How many people live in Champaign?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 88,302 residents. That makes Champaign the tenth most populous municipality in Illinois.
